newsitem.title: POLAND: Rightist May Day protesters anger Polish president.
newsitem.headline: Rightist May Day protesters anger Polish president.

text.p: Right-wing demonstrators on Thursday attempted to disrupt leftist Mayday celebrations around Poland, evoking angry comments from ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski.

"There are enough streets and squares for the League to celebrate where it wants and let the Democatic Left Alliance (SLD) and Polish Socialist Party (PPS) celebrate where they want," PAP news agency quoted Kwasniewski as saying.

Kwasniewski, a former SLD leader, was referring to the militantly anti-communist Republican League whose members unleashed abusive language, eggs, tomatoes and firecrackers against mostly elderly May Day marchers and scuffled with police in Warsaw and other cities.

"But if someone wants to pick a fight, it is the duty of law enforcement organs to thwart that design. Hence the detentions and questioning," Kwasniewski said following the detention of 75 mainly youthful right-wingers across the country.

"The Republican League is looking for trouble...in that sense it is no different than those who today have organised such actions in Paris or Germany, and these are usually extremist, right-wing, often Nazi groups," he added.

The Republican League is a small, mainly student group which wants former communists brought to book for their past abuses and regularly heckle Kwasniewski during his public appearances around the country.

Up to 2,000 members of leftist groups including the ex-communist Social Democrats (SdRP), dominant force in Poland's coalition government, marched to the sound of a brass band in Warsaw, as radical right-wing hecklers pelted them with insults and tomatoes.

The SdRP, which now supports democracy, fast European Union and NATO membership and market economics, sees itself as a Western-style social democratic party and has forgiven itself for its undemocratic communist antecedents.
One SdRP supporter carried a long red banner proclaiming "Good luck, Tony Blair".
In the central city of Lodz, young anti-communists who tried to satirise May Day celebrations were whisked away by police.
In Poznan, in the west, anti-leftists burnt a red flag, and their counterparts in the north-eastern city of Bialystok staged a mock-communist rally with portraits of Soviet founder Vladimir Lenin.
Despite the incidents, police said things were relatively calm.
"This year's May Day was far more peaceful than last year's," PAP reported national police spokesman Andrzej Przemyski as saying.
Thirty-nine people were detained in Warsaw, 17 in the southern town of Sosnowiec, 13 in Lodz and three each in Poznan and the western Baltic port of Szczecin, he added.
Some Solidarity union supporters around the country marked the traditional workers' holiday with Catholic church services in honour of St Joseph the Worker.
